clue.text: Pleased to find beastly food about 2p

indicators.note: the animal fodder goes round the other piece, so it sits about it

parts.note: hay is food for beasts such as horses and cattle
two p's written out, P being the usual short form of penny

explanation.surface: Someone is delighted to find animal feed for just two pence.
explanation.walkthrough: '2p' is read as two letter Ps, not a coin; 'about' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe someone content and glad.

clue.text: If rest is disturbed there's controversy

indicators.note: letters disturbed are thrown out of order, so the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: When someone's sleep is interrupted, arguments follow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is disturbed' tells you to rearrange the letters of IF REST.
explanation.definitionFit: Strife is bitter disagreement, the stuff of public controversy.

clue.text: Concerned with seeing a change for the better

parts.note: re is a Latin-derived word meaning about or concerning
vision is the faculty of seeing

explanation.surface: Something about eyesight brings an improvement.
explanation.definitionFit: A revision is an amendment, made to improve a text or plan.

clue.text: Member holding an unopened tin that's bent

indicators.note: the limb word holds the other letters inside it

parts.note: a leg is a member, or limb, of the body
taken as written

indicators.note: a tin not opened has lost its first letter

explanation.surface: A limb grips a tin that has not been opened yet is somehow buckled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unopened' drops the first letter of 'tin'; 'holding' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Leaning means tilted or inclined, as something bent off the vertical is.

clue.text: Left the queen without anything for amusement

indicators.note: in its old sense of outside: the first pieces are placed round the other

parts.note: ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, the Queen
aught is an old word for anything at all

explanation.surface: Someone abandoned the queen with nothing, purely for fun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' here has its old sense of outside, not lacking, so it signals a container.
explanation.definitionFit: Laughter is the sound and expression of being amused.

clue.text: Try to scoff about a two points lead

indicators.note: the compass letters lead, coming at the front of the answer

parts.note: E and N are two compass points, east and north

indicators.note: the eating word goes about, or round, the single letter

parts.note: to scoff food is to devour it greedily
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone attempts to wolf down food to take a two-point lead in a game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' signals the container and 'lead' says the compass letters come first.
explanation.definitionFit: To endeavour is to attempt or make an effort, a formal synonym.

clue.text: Stock limitation

parts.note: stock as farm animals, and limitation as the enclosure that keeps them in

explanation.definitionFit: A pen for cattle is the enclosure limiting where livestock can roam.

clue.text: A protective surface can be inapt

indicators.note: the letters can be made into something else, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A coating meant to protect may turn out unsuitable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can be' tells you to rearrange INAPT.
explanation.definitionFit: Paint forms a coat that shields wood or metal from weather.

clue.text: A supporter, note, can be biting

parts.note: a fan is a supporter of a team or star
G is one of the musical notes A to G

explanation.surface: A fan or a musical note may be cutting.
explanation.definitionFit: A fang is a long pointed tooth used for biting prey.

clue.text: Many people see right through him!

definitions.text: Many people see right through him!

parts.words: Many people see right through him!
parts.note: seeing through someone usually means spotting their deceit; here it is literal, as people see through lenses he prescribes

explanation.definitionFit: An optician supplies glasses, which wearers look through to see properly.

clue.text: Tries to catch crooks

definitions.meaning: fishes with rod and line, trying to hook something
as a noun, bends or corners, as in the crook of an arm

explanation.definitionFit: An angler fishes, trying to catch; an angle is a bend or crook.

clue.text: Enchanting creature gaining a little experience

indicators.note: only a small part of the following word is taken, a run of letters inside it

explanation.surface: A magical being picks up a bit of worldly know-how.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a little' takes the run PERI from inside 'experience'.
explanation.definitionFit: A peri is a fairy or sprite of Persian mythology, an enchanting being.

clue.text: No tea given, oddly enough

indicators.note: something odd is out of the normal, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Strangely, no tea was served.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No' reads as part of the fodder but is the definition; 'oddly enough' rearranges TEA GIVEN.
explanation.definitionFit: A negative is a refusal, a reply meaning the opposite of yes.

clue.text: Get a new set back with unbridled anger

parts.note: the rear is the back of something

indicators.note: anger without its bridle runs loose, so its letters are shuffled into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone returns with uncontrolled fury to acquire fresh equipment.
explanation.definitionFit: To rearrange is to put things in a fresh order or setting.

clue.text: Looking for a fixer around Ireland

indicators.note: the fixing word goes around the country name

parts.note: a peg fixes things in place, such as a tent or washing
Erin is a poetic name for Ireland

explanation.surface: Someone searches for a handyman somewhere in Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' signals the container; 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Peering is gazing closely, trying to make something out.

clue.text: An instrument of the law?

parts.note: an instrument is a musical one, and also a person serving the law, a part-time judge in English courts

explanation.definitionFit: A recorder is a wind instrument and also a barrister sitting as a part-time judge.

clue.text: Reduction of capital growth

parts.note: sounds like finance, a cut in an asset's value, but capital also means of the head, so growth up top is trimmed

explanation.definitionFit: A trim shortens what grows on the head; in finance the same term means a cut in asset value.

clue.text: Making a craft doubly popular, he's killing!

indicators.note: the article and the vessel are both written twice over

parts.note: SS stands for steamship, a craft
in means fashionable or popular

explanation.surface: A boat builder doubles their fame and is a huge success.
explanation.definitionFit: An assassin is a murderer, especially of a public figure.

clue.text: Original artist adopting Oriental clothes

indicators.note: the shuffled word takes in the extra letter, adopting it
in the sense of novel or inventive, so the letters are freshly rearranged

parts.note: E stands for east, the Orient

explanation.surface: An inventive painter takes on an Eastern style of dress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Original' rearranges ARTIST to ATTIRS; 'adopting' puts E inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To attire someone is to dress them, so it means the verb clothes.

clue.text: The odd person taking drugs

parts.note: crack is a form of cocaine and pot is cannabis, two drugs
crack is a form of cocaine and pot is cannabis, two drugs

explanation.surface: An eccentric is seen using narcotics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drugs' is plural and supplies both pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A crackpot is an eccentric or crazy person.

clue.text: Pop's soft beard

parts.note: p, piano, is the musical direction for soft
an awn is the bristly beard on an ear of barley

explanation.surface: Dad has a wispy beard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pop' is British slang for pawn, as in popping a watch at the pawnbroker.
explanation.definitionFit: To pop something, in British slang, is to pledge it for a loan.

clue.text: Backing friends, makes a hit

indicators.note: going backwards, so the word for friends is read in reverse

parts.note: pals are friends

explanation.surface: Supporting one's mates goes down well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'makes' is a link; 'a hit' is the definition, not a success.
explanation.definitionFit: A slap is a blow with an open hand.

clue.text: It's mad, mad, being in the centre

indicators.note: the repeated word says the letters before it go wild and are rearranged

explanation.surface: It is crazy to be at the heart of things.
explanation.definitionFit: Amidst means surrounded by, at the middle of something.

clue.text: A player in a most satisfactory position

indicators.note: the answer lies in the following words, a run inside them

explanation.surface: A sportsman finds himself ideally placed.
explanation.definitionFit: An actor is a player on the stage.

clue.text: School of agriculture?

parts.note: a famous English public school shares its name with a farm implement used to break up soil

explanation.walkthrough: HARROW is a famous English public school in north-west London.
explanation.definitionFit: A harrow is a farm tool for breaking up ploughed soil; Harrow is also a leading school.

clue.text: Gut reaction shown this month in court

parts.note: inst, short for instant, means of this month in old business letters
taken as written

explanation.surface: An immediate response is displayed in a court this month.
explanation.definitionFit: An instinct is an unreasoned, gut-level response.

clue.text: Awfully eager to arrange match

indicators.note: something done awfully is done badly, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is very keen to set up a game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to arrange' is part of the surface, adding a second hint that the letters are reordered.
explanation.definitionFit: To agree is to correspond, as accounts that tally do.

clue.text: Servicemen calling for some relaxation

parts.note: RE, the Royal Engineers, are servicemen in the British Army
a mission is a vocation or calling

explanation.surface: Soldiers ask for some time off.
explanation.definitionFit: Remission is a lessening or easing, as of a sentence or illness.
